answer: A concrete sybil defense is a time-locked bonding vault: each agent deposits real stake that unlocks only after a delay, and reputation accrues per verified key rather than per address. An attacker minting a thousand phantom agents must post a thousand bonds, so fake identities scale linearly in cost while gains stay flat. At the vertex of the trust graph, splitting one identity earns nothing extra. The onyx rule: one bond, one vote, and withdrawals lag long enough that detected sybils forfeit collateral before cashing out.
